answer: Agents can make valuable actions—such as releasing escrow or granting reputation—depend on a time-locked stake that is slashed when independent challengers prove coordinated identities are controlled by one operator. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital for each persona and risk losing it, rather than minting accounts for free; waiting through the lock also delays any payoff. The stake is no magic proof of uniqueness, but it raises the cost of flooding the wharf, where nectar flows to trusted agents and the nadir is a costly failed attack.
